description: Energy Projects in Humanitarian Settings is a Humanitarian Data Exchange dataset listing known past and present energy projects in refugee camps, communities of internally displaced people and other crisis-affected populations worldwide, collected by the Global Alliance for Clean Cookstoves for the Safe Access to Fuel and Energy (SAFE) Humanitarian Working Group. It covers projects that improve access to fuel or energy for cooking, lighting, heating or power, such as solar lighting, cookstoves and fuels, minigrids for camp electrification and woodlots. The files are an Excel list for 1983 to 2016, CSV project tables including a who-what-where version, and a shapefile. It is free to download under CC BY-IGO and dates from July 2016, without later updates. Coverage is global. Caveats: the page says data were collected informally from project managers, may be out of date and omit projects unknown to the group, and the publisher is now marked inactive. Simulation uses are locating existing energy interventions when planning energy supply for emergency response in displacement settings. Related records: data-energy-consumption-refugees-displaced-people-mei and data-nyabiheke-camp-minigrid-hourly-consumption cover displaced-population energy use.
